captions.detailed: A 3D-printable novelty 'love lock' featuring a rectangular solid lock body and a curved shackle or cable pin. The body is a thick, hollowed-out block with flat front and back faces, designed to accommodate custom engraved text. The shackle consists of two straight cylindrical legs topped with a segmented, curved arch made of small overlapping spheres. The shackle legs insert directly into two circular holes positioned on the top face of the lock body.
captions.instruction: Design a parametric 'love lock' in OpenSCAD with a customizable rectangular body and a flexible-looking cable pin. The body should support multiple lines of engraved text on its front face and include internal cylindrical cutouts for the shackle legs, while the pin should be composed of straight cylinders capped with an arched arrangement of spheres.
captions.factory: The code defines three modules: body(), pin(), and lever(). The body() module creates a hollow rectangular block using a difference of two cubes, subtracts two vertical cylinders for the shackle holes, and uses the external 'write' library to engrave four customizable text strings on the front face. The pin() module models the shackle by positioning a series of spheres in a semi-circular arch using a for-loop with sin/cos trigonometry, connected to two vertical cylinders that represent the straight legs of the cable. The lever() module creates small internal locking pins using cylinders and cubes rotated into place.
